html:
Ahmad Zahir (1946 to 1979) was an Afghan singer and composer, called the Elvis of Afghanistan and still the best loved voice of Afghan popular music. He was the son of Abdul Zahir, a royal physician who became prime minister in 1971.

He started in a high school band in Kabul in the 1960s, in the freer years that followed the constitution of 1964. He sang mostly in Dari Persian, and also in Pashto, setting the verses of classical poets to music that mixed Afghan folk, Indian classical, Persian and Western pop and rock, with harmonium, tabla, guitar and organ. He recorded at least fourteen albums.

His songs of love and loss became the sound of 1970s Kabul. After the communist coup of 1978 he fell out of favour with the new rulers. He died on his 33rd birthday in 1979 on the road near the Salang Pass, officially in a car crash; many believe he was murdered. Under the Taliban his grave in Kabul was damaged, but his songs are still played at Afghan weddings around the world, carried by the Afghan refugee exodus.
